data.title: Data-Flow and Call-Graph Analysis Evasion
data.summary: The sample routes a value through redundant arithmetic, opaque predicates or unused auxiliary variables so that automated data-flow and call-graph tools lose track of where a critical value actually originates.
data.description:
Where disassembler evasion targets instruction decoding, this targets the layer above it:
automated tools that try to answer 'where did this value come from' or 'what calls this
function' are defeated by indirection — a value passed through a chain of trivial
transformations that cancel out, or a call made through a computed address rather than a
direct reference, so the call graph shows no edge at all.
data.recommendation:
* Resolve indirect calls by tracing the computed target value at runtime rather than relying on a static call-graph tool.
* Simplify arithmetic chains symbolically (constant-fold and cancel redundant operations) before attempting manual data-flow analysis.
* Treat an unusually sparse call graph as evidence of this technique rather than evidence of a simple binary.
data.short_recommendation: Resolve indirect calls dynamically rather than relying on static call-graph tooling.
